title: Falcons DL Da'Shawn Hand believed to have torn quad after Week 1 injury
dek: Falcons defensive lineman Da'Shawn Hand exited Week 1 after playing only seven snaps with a knee injury. According to NFL Media's Ian Rapoport, Hand is believed to have a torn quadriceps that is expected to require season-ending surgery, though Hand is currently seeking additional medical opinions.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Da'Shawn Hand suffered a torn quadriceps in Week 1 that is believed to require season-ending surgery, according to NFL Media reporting.
bottom_line: Hand's decision on whether to undergo surgery will be confirmed once he completes his medical consultations. If season-ending surgery is performed, the Falcons will need to address the defensive line depth through roster additions and free agency moves.
body: Falcons defensive lineman Da'Shawn Hand sustained a torn quadriceps in Week 1 that is believed to require season-ending surgery, according to NFL Media's Ian Rapoport. Per Yahoo NFL, Hand played only seven snaps before exiting with a knee injury.

Hand is currently soliciting additional medical opinions before deciding on a course of action, meaning the season-ending surgery is not yet confirmed. He was one of the Falcons' larger offseason signings, added with an eye toward improving the team's run defense after the unit struggled in 2025.

The injury compounds Atlanta's defensive line challenges. According to the report, the Falcons have already lost Jalon Walker to a torn ACL and have James Pearce Jr. suspended for eight games. The remaining defensive linemen in rotation, Brandon Dorlus, LaCale London, Gervon Dexter, and Maason Smith, all performed well in Week 1, but none possess Hand's proven track record against the run.

The Falcons opened the 2026 season with a loss to the Steelers. Per the report, the team will almost certainly add either Zach Harrison or Zacch Pickens to the active roster and may pursue additional defensive line additions through free agency.
